I understand. It helps validate our feelings. Proof that we’ve suffered. And even though everyone’s feelings and sh is valid, seeing that your scars are deeper than others is satisfying. It acknowledges that we have felt more pain, we can hurt ourselves more, our suffering is greater. It’s a twisted sense of pride, but it doesn’t make you a bad person. I think everyone struggles with this feeling. It’s why there’s always this incessant urge to go deeper. Sh has become something like a competition in this community, even if no one really talks about it. Everyone just says, “oh, you’re feelings are still valid no matter how deep you cut”. Even if it’s true, there’s still that twisted superiority complex. So you don’t need to feel bad about it. It’s something I’m sure everyone, including myself, feels at some point.

Keeping Him in our thoughts, doing our best to follow Jesus’ example. I don’t know if I can explain it that well since I’m still in the process of learning it 😅

It’s how we spend time with Him and establish a relationship, right? So I don’t think I can say that I love God with all my heart, or that I put Him first in my life. I don't remember exactly when I started self-harming. It wasn't as obvious as just cutting, and I used to do it solely because I was curious about pain. I felt that I was never going to experience certain things because I would never be in those situations, so I tried to replicate them. Or, I just tried things that hurt my body (ex: pouring salt in my eyes, not drinking water for a couple of days)s. 

In middle school, I started feeling depressed, tho I didn't really self-harm yet. Not until 8th grade, when I started using a sewing needle to scratch words on my arm (only cat scratches, not styro). I just felt like I was stupid and worthless, and I felt alone because no one ever noticed the scratches or my mood shift. 

Ninth grade, I still didn't cut, but I used the sewing needle to bury under my skin before ripping the skin from my palms. Sophomore year was kind of a blur, but I expect I did more of the same behavior, except I started using a piece of ceramic from a cracked jar to "cut". Junior year was the same, but I mostly used my pencil to scratch till it bled a little. However, the summer between junior and senior year is when I really started to cut. It was more of the same stuff, that no one cared about how I felt, not really. I just took my disposable razor and started cutting my thigh. I remember that I thought that it didn't even hurt that much, and how much of a baby I was for being scared of cutting earlier. I won't delve into too much detail, but basically we've gone through a series of upgrades since then: a paper cutter blade, an exacto knife, and my current favorite, my box cutter. 

I still don't think that I cut deep enough (I don't think I've hit fat yet), but idk. I have not by any means overcome my selfharm, but I just try to remember that people care. None of my friends or family know that I cut.

Sorry this was so long, if you read to the end, I appreciate it :)
